title: Ezekiel Bible Quiz - Chapter 7
description: Ten questions on Ezekiel 7: the end on the four corners of the land, silver in the streets and no one going to battle.

questions.text: What does the Lord Yahweh say has come on the four corners of the land of Israel?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:2 says, "An end! The end has come on the four corners of the land."

answers.text: The end
A famine of seven years
A sword out of the north
The glory of Yahweh

questions.text: What does he say about his eye in verse 4?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:4 says, "My eye will not spare you, neither will I have pity," and that then they will know that I am Yahweh.

answers.text: It will watch over the righteous
It will not spare, and he will have no pity
It will turn away in sorrow
It will look for one man to spare the city

questions.text: What kind of day does verse 7 say is near on the mountains?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:7 says the time has come and the day is near, a day of tumult, and not of joyful shouting, on the mountains.

answers.text: A day of feasting and gladness
A day of rain and storm
A day of tumult, not of joyful shouting
A day of rest from their enemies

questions.text: According to verse 10, what has blossomed and what has budded?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:10 says the rod has blossomed and pride has budded.

answers.text: The vine has blossomed and the fig has budded
The almond has blossomed and the olive has budded
Peace has blossomed and joy has budded
The rod has blossomed and pride has budded

questions.text: What is said to the buyer and the seller in verse 12?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:12 says, "Don't let the buyer rejoice, nor the seller mourn; for wrath is on all its multitude."

answers.text: The buyer should mourn and the seller should rejoice
The buyer should not rejoice and the seller should not mourn
Both should sell their fields at once
Both should bring their silver to the temple

questions.text: What does verse 14 say happens, though they have blown the trumpet and made all ready?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:14 says they have blown the trumpet and made all ready, but no one goes to the battle, for God's wrath is on all its multitude.

answers.text: No one goes to the battle
The city gates were thrown open
The enemy army fled away
All the people gathered to fight

questions.text: What does verse 17 say about their hands and their knees?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:17 says all hands will be feeble and all knees will be weak as water.

answers.text: Their hands will be lifted and their knees bowed in prayer
Their hands will be bound with chains
Their hands will be full of silver
All hands will be feeble and all knees weak as water

questions.text: What will they do with their silver, and what will their gold become?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:19 says they will cast their silver in the streets, their gold will be as an unclean thing, and neither will be able to deliver them in the day of Yahweh's wrath.

answers.text: Give all of their silver and gold to the priests
Melt their silver and their gold down into idols
Cast the silver in the streets, and the gold will be an unclean thing
Hide their silver and gold inside the walls

questions.text: According to verse 26, what will perish from the priest and what from the elders?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:26 says they will seek a vision of the prophet, but the law will perish from the priest and counsel from the elders.

answers.text: Counsel from the priest, and the law from the elders
The law from the priest, and counsel from the elders
The vision from the priest, and the law from the elders
The incense from the priest, and the gate from the elders

questions.text: What does the last verse say will happen to the king and the prince?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:27 says the king will mourn, the prince will be clothed with desolation, and the hands of the people of the land will be troubled.

answers.text: The king will flee to Egypt with his princes
The prince will be made a servant in Babylon
The king will be struck blind in his own house
The king will mourn and the prince will be clothed with desolation
